title: At a mass ratio of 15/18, two HD 93683 eclipse fits exceed the spin budget if both spin capacities are at most 0.075
abstract: We test whether the two inner stellar spins can supply the plane change in two published HD 93683 eclipse fits without an external torque. Angular momentum conservation gives Smax/Lmin >= sin(theta/2). We apply a lower bound on theta that permits the photometric ambiguity between i and 180 degrees minus i. At a mass ratio of 15/18 and the fitted fractional radii, the fits require a common normalized spin capacity of at least 0.0862 and 0.0893. A capacity of 0.075 for each star is insufficient. Here capacity is spin angular momentum divided by m sqrt(G m R); for rigid rotation it is the gyration coefficient times the fraction of spherical critical rotation. We also give a lower bound on external angular impulse. The stronger signed drift test requires capacities of 0.1273 and 0.1318, but its branch choice is not fixed by spherical eclipse photometry alone. The exclusion is conditional: mass-ratio and radius changes weaken it, and neither spin capacity is measured. We add no new photometry or companion detection. Code, aggregate source inputs, hashes, figures and numerical checks are included.
